description:
Pounce puts your AI coding agents in your pocket.

Start Pounce on your computer, scan the pairing code, and every agent session running there appears on your phone. Watch them think, write code, run commands, and open pull requests in real time — then step in whenever you want.

WHAT YOU CAN DO
• Follow every session live — messages, reasoning, tool calls, terminal output and git activity in one clean timeline
• Review the diff, then commit, push, or open a pull request
• Send a new instruction or answer a prompt with a tap
• Use your voice — hold and speak to steer an agent hands-free
• See where your usage goes — tokens, spend, sessions and messages, broken down by agent, by model and by project
• Keep every machine and project in one list, sorted by what needs you

WORKS WITH
Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and opencode.

HOW IT WORKS
1. Start Pounce on your Mac, Windows or Linux machine — the desktop app, or a single command in any terminal
2. Scan the pairing code with Pounce
3. Your agents and projects appear automatically

REACH IT FROM ANYWHERE
Pounce connects straight to your own computer over an encrypted peer-to-peer link. That works on cellular or a café network with no VPN and no port forwarding, and your code and conversations never pass through a server of ours.

Pounce is open source under the MIT license.

Whether you're grabbing coffee, on the couch, or away from your laptop, Pounce keeps your agents moving.
promotionalText: Now with usage insights: see tokens, spend, sessions and messages per agent, per model and per project — for a week, a month, or a year.
whatsNew:
Usage insights
Activity now shows what your agents actually use — tokens, estimated spend, sessions and messages — for a week, a month or a year.

Tap any figure to open it up: a trend over time, then a breakdown by agent, by model, and by project.

Token counts now come straight from each agent's own records, so they match the figure your provider shows you. The share that was re-read from cache sits alongside the total, because on a long session most of it is cache — and that part is cheap.

Also in this release: faster thread loading, and a steadier layout when switching between week, month and year.
